h: Noach, the Generations, and the Purpose of Torah
The Flood generation, Noah’s righteousness, and the eventual reception of Torah reveal the path of human repair.
These Are the Generations of Noach

p: "אֵלֶּה תּוֹלְדֹת נֹחַ".
— "These are the generations of Noah."
בְּתַנְחוּמָא (פָּרָשַׁת נֹחַ א) פָּתַח:
— In Midrash Tanchuma (Parashat Noach 1) it opens:
"יִתְבָּרַךְ שְׁמוֹ שֶׁל מֶלֶךְ מַלְכֵי הַמְּלָכִים הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא שֶׁבָּחַר בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל וְכוּלֵי,
— 'Blessed be the Name of the King of kings, the Holy One, blessed be He, Who chose Israel, etc.,
וְנָתַן לָנוּ הַתּוֹרָה בִּכְתָב בְּרֶמֶז, צְפוּנוֹת וּסְתוּמוֹת,
— and gave us the Written Torah with hinted, concealed, and veiled teachings,
וּפֵירְשׁוּם בְּתוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה וְכוּלֵי",
— and explained them in the Oral Torah, etc.',
וְהֶאֱרִיךְ בְּעִנְיַן תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה, עַיֵּין שָׁם.
— and elaborated extensively upon the Oral Torah, see there.
וְיֵשׁ לְהָבִין שַׁיָּיכוּת עִנְיַן תּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב וְתוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה לְהַפָּרָשָׁה.
— And one must understand the connection of the Written Torah and Oral Torah to this parashah.
וְיוּבַן עַל פִּי מַה שֶׁשָּׁנִינוּ (פֶּרֶק ה דְּאָבוֹת מִשְׁנָה ב):
— And it will be understood based on what we learned (Avot 5:2):
עֲשָׂרָה דוֹרוֹת מֵאָדָם וְעַד נֹחַ,
— There were ten generations from Adam until Noah,
לְהוֹדִיעַ כַּמָּה אֶרֶךְ אַפַּיִם לְפָנָיו וְכוּלֵי;
— to make known how great is His patience, etc.;
עֲשָׂרָה דוֹרוֹת מִנֹּחַ וְעַד אַבְרָהָם וְכוּלֵי,
— ten generations from Noah until Abraham, etc.,
עַד שֶׁבָּא אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ וְקִבֵּל שְׂכַר כּוּלָּם.
— until Abraham our father came and received the reward of them all.
וְהִנֵּה בְּכָל מָקוֹם מִסְפַּר עֲשָׂרָה הוּא כְּנֶגֶד עֲשֶׂרֶת הַדִּבְּרוֹת,
— Now behold, in every context the number ten corresponds to the Ten Commandments,
שֶׁהֵם מְכֻוָּונִים נֶגֶד עֶשֶׂר סְפִירוֹת
— which correspond to the Ten Sefirot
שֶׁהֶאֱצִיל הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ לִבְרִיאַת הָעוֹלָם.
— that Hashem, blessed be He, emanated for the creation of the world.
וְהָיוּ עֲשָׂרָה דוֹרוֹת מֵאָדָם וְעַד נֹחַ
— And there were ten generations from Adam to Noah
לְתַקֵּן כָּל פְּגַם קִלְקוּל אָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן
— to rectify the entire blemish of Adam the First's sin
וּלְהִתְבָּרֵר בְּכָל הַמִּדּוֹת;
— and to become refined in all character traits;
וְאָז בְּדוֹר הַמַּבּוּל הָיָה רָאוּי לְמַתַּן תּוֹרָה,
— and then, in the Generation of the Flood, it was originally fit for the Giving of the Torah,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּמִּדְרָשׁ רַבָּה (מִשְׁפָּטִים פָּרָשָׁה ל)
— as written in Midrash Rabbah (Mishpatim, Parashah 30)
וּבַזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק ג, רטז עַמּוּד ב),
— and in the holy Zohar (Part III, 216b),
וְהָיָה אָז נֶפֶשׁ מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ,
— and the soul of Moses our teacher was present then,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנִּרְמַז: "בְּשַׁגַּם" – בְּגִימַטְרִיָּא מֹשֶׁה.
— as hinted: 'be-shagam' (בְּשַׁגַּם = 345) has the gematria of Moshe (מֹשֶׁה = 345).
וְהָיוּ זוֹכִין לְתוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב וְתוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה
— And they would have merited the Written Torah and the Oral Torah,
שֶׁנִּרְמְזוּ בְּמַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר:
— which were hinted at in that which is stated:
"נִבְקְעוּ כָּל מַעְיְנֹת תְּהוֹם רַבָּה"
— ‘all the fountains of the great deep burst open’—
מַבּוּעֵי דְּחָכְמְתָא לְתַתָּא,
— the wellsprings of wisdom below (the Oral Torah),
"וַאֲרֻבֹּת הַשָּׁמַיִם נִפְתָּחוּ"
— ‘and the windows of heaven were opened’—
תַּרְעֵי דְּחָכְמְתָא לְעֵילָּא,
— the gates of wisdom above (the Written Torah),
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק א, קיז עַמּוּד א),
— as written in the holy Zohar (Part I, 117a),
וְאָז הָיוּ מְתַקְּנִים כָּל פְּגַם הַנָּחָשׁ כְּמוֹ שֶׁיִּהְיֶה לֶעָתִיד.
— and then they would have rectified the entire blemish of the Serpent as will be in the ultimate future.
וְעַל יְדֵי שֶׁהָיוּ מַכְעִיסִין לְפָנָיו
— Yet through their continually provoking Him,
נֶהֶפְכוּ לְמַיִם הַזֵּידוֹנִים
— these waters were transformed into raging waters,
וְנִשְׁטְפוּ כוּלָּם בְּמֵי הַמַּבּוּל
— and they were all washed away in the waters of the Flood,
וְלֹא נִשְׁאַר מֵהֶם רַק נֹחַ.
— and none remained of them except Noah.
וּמִטַּעַם זֶה נֶחְשְׁבוּ בַּעֲשָׂרָה דוֹרוֹת שֶׁקּוֹדֶם הַמַּבּוּל
— And for this reason, in the ten generations before the Flood,
בְּכָל אֶחָד חֶשְׁבּוֹן הַכּוֹלֵל כָּל יְמֵי חַיֵּיהֶם,
— there is calculated for each person a sum total encompassing all the days of their lives,
מִפְּנֵי שֶׁבַּחַיִּים שֶׁחָיוּ אַחַר שֶׁהוֹלִידוּ רֹאשׁ הַדּוֹר
— because in the life they lived after fathering the head of the generation,
לֹא הָיָה לָהֶם חַיִּים מְחוּדָּשׁ,
— they possessed no renewed, independent life;
שֶׁכָּל עִיקַּר הַחַיִּים שֶׁלָּהֶם הָיָה רַק שֶׁיֵּצֵא אֶחָד הַנֶּחְשָׁב בְּחֶשְׁבּוֹן הַדּוֹרוֹת
— for the entire essence of their life was merely that one person emerge who counted in the tally of generations,
שֶׁמִּזֶּה יָצָא נֹחַ וְנִבְנָה הָעוֹלָם;
— from whom Noah emerged and the world was rebuilt;
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן מַה שֶּׁחָיוּ אַחַר כָּךְ וְהוֹלִידוּ בָּנִים וּבָנוֹת,
— whereas from what they lived afterward and fathered sons and daughters,
מִזֶּה לֹא נִשְׁאַר שׁוּם הַשְׁאָרָה, שֶׁהֲרֵי נִשְׁטְפוּ בַּמַּבּוּל.
— no remnant survived from this, since they were wiped out in the Flood.
וְנִכְלְלוּ הַחַיִּים שֶׁחָיוּ אַחַר שֶׁהוֹלִידוּ רֹאשׁ הַדּוֹר
— And the life they lived after fathering the head of the generation was subsumed
עִם הַחַיִּים שֶׁחָיוּ קוֹדֶם,
— with the life they lived beforehand,
וְעַל יְדֵי כֵן נִקְרְאוּ בִּלְשׁוֹן חַיִּים;
— and through this they were termed with the terminology of 'life';
וְכֵיוָן שֶׁנִּכְלְלוּ כָּל יְמֵי חַיֵּיהֶם יַחַד, כְּתִיב "וַיָּמֹת".
— and since all the days of their lives were tallied together, it is written 'and he died.'
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן בַּעֲשָׂרָה דוֹרוֹת שֶׁמִּנֹּחַ וְעַד אַבְרָהָם שֶׁבְּפָרָשָׁה זוֹ,
— In contrast, in the ten generations from Noah to Abraham in this parashah,
שֶׁנִּשְׁאַר גַּם מִמַּה שֶּׁהוֹלִידוּ
— remnants survived also from what was fathered
אַחַר שֶׁהוֹלִידוּ רֹאשׁ הַדּוֹר,
— after they fathered the head of the generation;
שֶׁמֵּהַבָּנִים וּבָנוֹת נִשְׁאֲרוּ אוּמּוֹת,
— for from the sons and daughters nations survived,
וְיֵשׁ בָּהֶם חַיִּים, כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "וְאַתָּה מְחַיֶּה אֶת כֻּלָּם", כַּיָּדוּעַ,
— and they possess vitality, as stated: 'and You preserve them all,' as is known;
אֲבָל אֵינָם דּוֹמִים לְהַחַיִּים שֶׁחָיוּ קוֹדֶם שֶׁהוֹלִידוּ רֹאשׁ הַדּוֹר
— yet they are not comparable to the life lived before fathering the head of the generation,
שֶׁמִּזֶּה נִשְׁתַּלְשֵׁל וְיָצָא אַבְרָהָם וְזַרְעוֹ, שֶׁהֵם חַיֵּי עוֹלָם.
— from which descended and emerged Abraham and his seed, who are eternal life.
וְכֵיוָן שֶׁאֵין שְׁנֵי הַחַיִּים דּוֹמִים זֶה לָזֶה,
— And since the two lifespans are not comparable to one another,
עַל כֵּן לֹא נִכְלַל בָּהֶם יַחַד הַחַיִּים שֶׁחָיוּ מִקּוֹדֶם עִם הַחַיִּים שֶׁחָיוּ אַחַר כָּךְ;
— therefore the life lived beforehand was not combined together with the life lived afterward;
וְכֵיוָן שֶׁלֹּא נִכְלְלוּ כָּל יְמֵי חַיֵּיהֶם יַחַד,
— and since all the days of their lives were not calculated together,
לָכֵן לֹא כְּתִיב בְּהוּ "וַיָּמֹת".
— therefore 'and he died' is not written regarding them.
זוּלַת בְּנֹחַ שֶׁלֹּא הוֹלִיד כְּלָל אַחַר הַמַּבּוּל,
— Except regarding Noah, who did not father any children at all after the Flood,
וְנִכְלְלוּ הַחַיִּים שֶׁחַי אַחַר הַמַּבּוּל
— and the life he lived after the Flood was subsumed
בִּכְלַל הַחַיִּים שֶׁחַי עַד שֶׁהוֹלִיד שֵׁם, חָם וָיֶפֶת,
— within the lifespan he lived until fathering Shem, Ham, and Japheth,
שֶׁמֵּהֶם נִבְנָה הָעוֹלָם,
— from whom the world was built,
וְלֹא הָיָה לְהַשָּׁנִים שֶׁחַי אַחַר כָּךְ חַיִּים מְחוּדָּשׁ;
— and the years he lived afterward did not constitute a separate, renewed line of vitality;
וְעַל כֵּן כְּתִיב בּוֹ: "וַיְהִי כָּל יְמֵי נֹחַ וְגוֹמֵר וַיָּמֹת".
— therefore it is written regarding him: 'And all the days of Noah were, etc., and he died.'
וְכֵן בְּתֶרַח, שֶׁאַחַר שֶׁחַי שִׁבְעִים שָׁנָה וְהוֹלִיד אַבְרָם, נָחוֹר וְהָרָן,
— And likewise with Terah, who after living seventy years and fathering Abram, Nahor, and Haran,
לֹא הוֹלִיד כְּלָל,
— did not father any further children,
וְלֹא הָיוּ בְּחַיָּיו שֶׁחַי אַחַר כָּךְ שׁוֹרֶשׁ חַיִּים מְחוּדָּשׁ בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ,
— and there was not in the life he lived afterward any separate renewed root of vitality,
וְעַל כֵּן נִכְלְלוּ כָּל יָמָיו יַחַד, וּכְתִיב: "וַיָּמָת תֶּרַח בְּחָרָן".
— and therefore all his days were calculated together, and it is written: 'and Terah died in Haran.'
וְכֵן הָעֲשָׂרָה דוֹרוֹת שֶׁמִּנֹּחַ וְעַד אַבְרָהָם הֵם גַּם כֵּן בְּמִסְפַּר עֶשֶׂר,
— And likewise the ten generations from Noah to Abraham are also in the number ten,
שֶׁהָיָה רָאוּי לְתַקֵּן כָּל הַפְּגָם.
— being fit to rectify the entire blemish.
וְאָמַר "לְהוֹדִיעַ וְכוּלֵי"
— And the Mishnah states 'to make known, etc.'
שֶׁכָּל הַדּוֹרוֹת הָיוּ מַכְעִיסִין וּבָאִין
— that all the generations went on provoking Him,
עַד שֶׁבָּא אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ וְקִבֵּל שְׂכַר כּוּלָּם,
— until Abraham our father came and received the reward of them all,
מַה שֶּׁלֹּא אָמַר מִקּוֹדֶם;
— which the Mishnah did not say regarding the earlier ten generations;
שֶׁמֵּעֲשָׂרָה דוֹרוֹת אֵלּוּ נִשְׁאַר הַשְׁאָרָה,
— for from these ten generations a spiritual remnant endured,
וְכָל הַנִּיצוֹצוֹת הַקְּדוֹשׁוֹת שֶׁהָיָה בָּהֶם קִבֵּל אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם,
— and all the holy sparks that were within them Abraham our father received;
שֶׁהוּא נִתְנַסָּה בַּעֲשָׂרָה נִסְיוֹנוֹת שֶׁהֵם גַּם כֵּן כְּנֶגֶד עֶשֶׂר סְפִירוֹת,
— in that he was tested with ten trials, which likewise correspond to the Ten Sefirot,
וְעָמַד בְּכוּלָּם וְנִתְבָּרֵר בְּכָל הַמִּדּוֹת.
— and he withstood them all and became refined in all character traits.
וְהוּא זָכָה שֶׁקִּיֵּים כָּל הַתּוֹרָה כֻּלָּהּ עַד שֶׁלֹּא נִתְּנָה (כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר יוֹמָא כח:),
— And he merited to fulfill the entire Torah before it was given (as stated in Yoma 28b),
וְהַיְינוּ אַף תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ שָׁם: "אֲפִילּוּ עֵירוּבֵי תַּבְשִׁילִין".
— meaning even the Oral Torah, as they said there: 'even Eiruv Tavshilin.'
וְגַם כָּל הַתּוֹרָה כֻּלָּהּ,
— Moreover, the entire Torah as a whole,
כֵּיוָן שֶׁלֹּא נִצְטַוָּה עָלֶיהָ,
— since he was not explicitly commanded concerning it,
רַק נַעֲשׂוּ שְׁתֵּי כִּלְיוֹתָיו כְּמִין שְׁנֵי רַבָּנִים
— rather his two kidneys were transformed like two rabbis
וְהָיוּ נוֹבְעוֹת וּמְלַמְּדוֹת אוֹתוֹ תּוֹרָה וְחָכְמָה,
— welling forth and teaching him Torah and wisdom,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה סא),
— as stated (Bereishit Rabbah, Parashah 61),
וְהוּא בְּחִינַת תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה
— and this is the aspect of the Oral Torah
שֶׁנּוֹבֵעַ בַּלֵּב מִדִּבְרֵי אֱלֹהִים חַיִּים.
— which wells up in the heart from the words of the living God.
וְזֶה שֶׁאָמַר בְּתַנְחוּמָא אַחַר כָּךְ בְּמַעֲלַת תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה:
— And this is what the Tanchuma stated afterward concerning the preeminence of the Oral Torah:
"לְפִי שֶׁאֵין לוֹמֵד אוֹתָהּ
— ‘Because no one learns it
אֶלָּא מִי שֶׁאוֹהֵב הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא בְּכָל לִבּוֹ וּבְכָל נַפְשׁוֹ וּבְכָל מְאֹדוֹ וְכוּלֵי",
— except one who loves the Holy One, blessed be He, with all his heart, with all his soul, and with all his might, etc.’;
וְאַהֲבָה מִדַּת אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם,
— and love is the attribute of Abraham our father, peace be upon him,
דִּכְתִיב: "אַבְרָהָם אֹהֲבִי",
— as it is written: 'Abraham My beloved,'
וְאָהַב הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא בְּכָל לִבּוֹ וּבְכָל נַפְשׁוֹ וּבְכָל מְאֹדוֹ,
— and he loved the Holy One with all his heart, all his soul, and all his might,
וְזָכָה לְתוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה.
— and merited the Oral Torah.
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁבְּדוֹר הַמַּבּוּל הָיָה הַזְּמַן שֶׁתִּנָּתֵן תּוֹרָה עַל יְדֵי נֶפֶשׁ מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ,
— And just as in the Generation of the Flood it was the time for Torah to be given through the soul of Moses our teacher,
וְהַיְינוּ תּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב שֶׁהָיָה כָּלוּל בָּהּ גַּם תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה,
— namely the Written Torah within which the Oral Torah was also enfolded,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁהָיָה בְּמַתַּן תּוֹרָה;
— just as occurred at the Giving of the Torah;
כֵּן בְּדוֹר הַפַּלָּגָה הָיָה הַזְּמַן לְהִתְגַּלּוּת הִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה.
— so in the Generation of the Dispersion (Dor HaFlagah) it was the time for the revelation and expansion of the Oral Torah.
וְעִיקַּר הִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה הָיָה בְּבָבֶל,
— And the primary expansion of the Oral Torah was in Babylonia,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (סֻכָּה כ עַמּוּד א);
— as they said (Sukkah 20a);
וְעַל כֵּן כְּשֶׁהִרְגִּישׁוּ בְּשִׁנְעָר מָקוֹם הָרָאוּי לְהִתְגַּלּוּת הִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה,
— therefore when they sensed in Shinar that it was a place fit for the revelation and expansion of the Oral Torah,
עָשׂוּ הֵם מִגְדָּל לְעוּמַּת בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ,
— they built a tower counter to the Holy Temple,
שֶׁהוּא מָקוֹם שֶׁמִּשָּׁם יוֹצֵאת תּוֹרָה לְכָל יִשְׂרָאֵל
— which is the place whence Torah goes forth to all Israel
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר סַנְהֶדְרִין פו:);
— (as stated in Sanhedrin 86b);
וְעָשׂוּ הֵם בְּ'זֶה לְעֻמַּת זֶה' מִגְדָּל לְהִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת הַבְלֵיהֶם.
— and they made, in parallel 'one corresponding to the other,' a tower for the expansion of their vanities.
וְאָז הָיָה אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם בֶּן אַרְבָּעִים וּשְׁמוֹנֶה שָׁנָה,
— And at that time Abraham our father, peace be upon him, was forty-eight years old,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַב רַשִׁ״י (שַׁבָּת י: דִּבּוּר הַמַּתְחִיל 'שֶׁיְּשִׁיבָתָהּ');
— as Rashi wrote (Shabbat 10b, s.v. she-yeshivatah);
וְאָז הִכִּיר אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם אֶת בּוֹרְאוֹ,
— and then Abraham our father recognized his Creator,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה ל);
— as written (Bereishit Rabbah, Parashah 30);
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁזָּכָה לְכָל הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה.
— meaning that he merited the entire Oral Torah.
וְאַחַר כָּךְ אַרְבַּע שָׁנִים עַד שֶׁהִתְחִיל שְׁנֵי אֲלָפִים תּוֹרָה.
— And afterward there were four years until the two thousand years of Torah began.
וְהָאַרְבַּע שָׁנִים שֶׁקָּדְמוּ
— And the four years that preceded
הֵם כְּנֶגֶד שָׁלֹשׁ רִאשׁוֹנוֹת וּמִדַּת חֶסֶד שֶׁהִיא מִדָּתוֹ שֶׁל אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם;
— correspond to the first three Sefirot and the attribute of Chesed, which is the attribute of Abraham our father, peace be upon him;
וְאַחַר כָּךְ הִתְחִיל הַשְּׁנֵי אֲלָפִים תּוֹרָה בְּמִדַּת גְּבוּרָה,
— and afterward began the two thousand years of Torah in the attribute of Gevurah,
דְּאוֹרַיְיתָא מִסִּטְרָא דִּגְבוּרָה קָא אָתְיָא
— for the Torah comes from the side of Gevurah
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר זֹהַר חֵלֶק ג, פ עַמּוּד ב),
— (as stated in Zohar Part III, 80b),
וְהַיְינוּ תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה,
— and this refers to the Oral Torah,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בַּתִּיקּוּנִים (תִּיקּוּן כא) וּבַזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק ב, קסז עַמּוּד א):
— as stated in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 21) and in the holy Zohar (Part II, 167a):
"וּמִשְּׂמָאלָא אִתְיְהִיבַת אוֹרַיְיתָא דִּבְעַל פֶּה".
— ‘and from the left was given the Oral Torah’.
וְזֶה שֶׁאָמַר: "עַד שֶׁבָּא אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ וְקִבֵּל שְׂכַר כּוּלָּם",
— And this is what it said: ‘until Abraham our father came and received the reward of them all’—
וְהַיְינוּ הַנִּיצוֹצוֹת הַקְּדוֹשׁוֹת וְהַחַיִּים שֶׁלָּהֶם,
— meaning their holy sparks and their vitality,
שֶׁהוּא קְדוּשַּׁת תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה,
— which is the holiness of the Oral Torah,
וְזָכָה בָּהּ אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם.
— and Abraham our father merited it.
וְזֶה שֶׁכָּתַב פֵּירוּשׁ רַשִׁ״י:
— And this is what Rashi wrote in his commentary:
"עַד אַבְרָם חֲרוֹן אַף שֶׁל מָקוֹם",
— 'until Abram there was the burning wrath of the Omnipresent',
דְּכֵיוָן שֶׁבָּא אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם לֹא הָיָה עוֹד חֲרוֹן אַף,
— for once Abraham our father came there was no longer burning wrath,
שֶׁזָּכָה וְנָטַל שְׂכַר כּוּלָּם,
— since he merited and took the reward of them all,
וְנִכְתַּב אַחַר נִסָּיוֹן הָרִאשׁוֹן;
— and this was written after the first trial;
וְזֶה שֶׁאָמַר: "לְהוֹדִיעַ כַּמָּה אֶרֶךְ אַפַּיִם לְפָנָיו וְכוּלֵי".
— and this is what the Mishnah meant by: ‘to make known how great is His patience, etc.’
וּבְתוֹסְפוֹת יוֹם טוֹב כָּתַב שֶׁיֵּשׁ שְׁנֵי מִינֵי אַף:
— And in Tosafot Yom Tov he wrote that there are two kinds of wrath:
יֵשׁ שֶׁמַּאֲרִיךְ וּלְבַסּוֹף מַשְׁחִית הַכֹּל כְּמוֹ בַּמַּבּוּל,
— there is one where He delays anger and in the end destroys everything as in the Flood,
וְיֵשׁ שֶׁמַּאֲרִיךְ שֶׁאֵינוֹ יוֹצֵא לַפּוֹעַל לִכְלָיוֹן חָרוּץ וְכוּלֵי.
— and there is one where He delays anger and it does not come to fruition in total destruction, etc.
וְהָרַב הַקָּדוֹשׁ זֵכֶר צַדִּיק וְקָדוֹשׁ לִבְרָכָה
— And the holy master of blessed memory
אָמַר בְּשֵׁם הָרַב הַקָּדוֹשׁ מִלּוּבְּלִין זֵכֶר צַדִּיק וְקָדוֹשׁ לִבְרָכָה,
— said in the name of the holy master of Lublin of blessed memory,
שֶׁפֵּירֵשׁ בְּמַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ:
— who explained that which our Sages said:
"כָּל מִי שֶׁאוֹמֵר הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא וַתְּרָן הוּא יִתְוַותְּרוּ בְּנֵי מֵעוֹהִי,
— ‘Whoever says that the Holy One, blessed be He, overlooks sins, his entrails shall be surrendered,
אֶלָּא מַאֲרִיךְ אַפֵּיהּ וְגָבֵי דִּילֵיהּ",
— rather He is patient and collects what is His’—
שֶׁהַפֵּירוּשׁ: וּמַגְבִּיהַּ דִּילֵיהּ הָאַף.
— that the meaning is: He raises up His wrath.
וְהִנֵּה מַאֲמָר זֶה נִזְכַּר בַּמִּדְרָשׁ (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה סז)
— Now this dictum is mentioned in the Midrash (Bereishit Rabbah, Parashah 67)
לְעִנְיַן צְעָקָה אַחַת הִזְעִיק יַעֲקֹב לְעֵשָׂו וְכוּלֵי
— regarding the single cry that Jacob caused Esau to utter, etc.,
וְהֵיכָן נִפְרַע לוֹ, עַיֵּין שָׁם,
— and where he was held accountable, see there,
וְשָׁם הַגִּרְסָא: "מַאֲרִיךְ אַפֵּיהּ וְגָבֵי דִּילֵיהּ";
— and there the reading is: ‘He is patient and collects what is His’;
וְכֵן הוּזְכַּר בַּיְרוּשַׁלְמִי (שְׁקָלִים פֶּרֶק ה הֲלָכָה ד)
— and so it is mentioned in the Yerushalmi (Shekalim 5:4)
לְעִנְיַן נְחוּנְיָא חוֹפֵר שִׁיחִין שֶׁמֵּת בְּנוֹ בַּצָּמָא,
— regarding Nechunya the well-digger whose son died of thirst,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר גַּם בְּתַלְמוּדֵנוּ (בָּבָא קַמָּא נ.),
— and as stated also in our Babylonian Talmud (Bava Kamma 50a),
וְשָׁם הַגִּרְסָא: "מַאֲרִיךְ רוּחֵיהּ וְגָבֵי דִּידֵיהּ".
— and there the text reads: ‘He is patient and collects what is His.’
וּבִשְׁנֵי הַמְּקוֹמוֹת מַשְׁמָע דְּפֵירוּשׁ "וְגָבֵי דִּילֵיהּ"
— And in both places it implies that the meaning of 've-gavei deileih' is:
שֶׁגּוֹבֶה אַחַר כָּךְ שֶׁלּוֹ לְשַׁלֵּם לוֹ גְּמוּל.
— that He collects His due afterward to repay him.
וּבְוַדַּאי דִּבְרֵי הָרַב הַקָּדוֹשׁ זִכְרוֹנוֹ לִבְרָכָה אֱמֶת.
— And certainly the words of the holy master of blessed memory are true.
וּלְפִי הָאָמוּר שְׁנֵיהֶם אֱמֶת:
— And according to what was explained, both interpretations are true:
דְּ"גָבֵי דִּילֵיהּ" – שֶׁמַּגְבִּיהַּ דִּילֵיהּ,
— for 've-gavei deileih' means He elevates His own,
כְּמוֹ כָּאן בְּאַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם שֶׁקִּבֵּל שְׂכַר כּוּלָּם
— just as here with Abraham our father who received the reward of them all
וְזָכָה לְכָל הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה שֶׁל דּוֹר הַפַּלָּגָה,
— and merited the entire Oral Torah of the Generation of the Dispersion,
וְנִסְתַּלֵּק חֲרוֹן אַף מִן הָעוֹלָם;
— and burning wrath was removed from the world;
וּמִמֵּילָא גּוֹבֶה שֶׁלּוֹ,
— and automatically He collects His due,
דְּכֵיוָן שֶׁקִּבֵּל מֵהֶם שׁוֹרֶשׁ הַחַיִּים שֶׁלָּהֶם וְהַנִּיצוֹצוֹת הַקְּדוֹשׁוֹת שֶׁבָּהֶם
— for once he received from them their root vitality and the holy sparks within them
בְּסוֹד "וְאַתָּה מְחַיֶּה אֶת כֻּלָּם",
— in the mystical secret of 'and You preserve them all,'
נֶעֱקַר חַיֵּיהֶם מִן הָעוֹלָם.
— their vitality was uprooted from the world.
וְזֶה שֶׁאָמַר: "לְהוֹדִיעַ כַּמָּה אֶרֶךְ אַפַּיִם לְפָנָיו וְכוּלֵי", וְכָאָמוּר.
— And this is what it meant: 'to make known how great is His patience, etc.,' and as explained.
וְזֶה עִנְיַן שַׁיָּיכוּת מַאֲמָר זֶה לְפָרָשַׁת "אֵלֶּה תּוֹלְדֹת נֹחַ",
— And this is the connection of this teaching to Parashat Toldot Noach:
שֶׁעִיקַּר הַפָּרָשָׁה הוּא אֵיךְ שֶׁקִּבֵּל אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה
— that the core of the parashah is how Abraham our father received the Oral Torah
שֶׁהָיָה בְּדוֹר הַפַּלָּגָה.
— which was intended for the Generation of the Dispersion.
וּבְשַׁבָּת הוּא זְמַן תּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב,
— And on Shabbat is the time of the Written Torah,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (שַׁבָּת פו:):
— as they said (Shabbat 86b):
"דְּכוּלֵי עָלְמָא בְּשַׁבָּת נִתְּנָה תּוֹרָה לְיִשְׂרָאֵל",
— ‘for all agree that on Shabbat the Torah was given to Israel’,
וּזְמַן רִבּוּי בְּתוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה,
— and it is the time of abundance in the Oral Torah,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק א, מז עַמּוּד ב):
— as stated in the holy Zohar (Part I, 47b):

paragraphs.text: Bereshit Rabbah 30:8: ““Faultless [tamim] in his generations” – bar Ḥatya said: Everyone in whose regard tamim is stated, he completed his years to a multiple of seven. “Was [haya]” – Rabbi Yoḥanan said: Anyone in whose regard haya is stated, he was righteous from beginning to end. They raised an objection against him: But is it not written: “Abraham was (haya) one, and he inherited the land” (Ezekiel 33:24); was he the same from beginning to end? He said to them: This, too, is not a contradiction, as Rabbi Levi said in the name of Reish Lakish: At the age of three years, Abraham recognized his Creator. Rabbi Ḥanina and Rabbi Yoḥanan, both of them say: At the age of forty-eight years, Abraham recognized his Creator. How, then, do I explain “haya”? It means that he was destined to guide the entire world to repent. [Similarly,] “Behold, man [Adam] has become [haya]” (Genesis 3:22) – he was destined for death. “The serpent was [haya]” (Genesis 3:1) – he was destined for calamity. “Cain was [haya]” (Genesis 4:2) – he was destined for exile. “Job was [haya]” (Job 1:1) – he was destined for suffering. “Noah was [haya]” – he was destined for a miracle. “Moses was [haya]” (Exodus 3:1) – he was destined to be a redeemer. “Mordekhai was [haya]” (Esther 2:5) – he was destined for redemption. Rabbi Levi and the other Rabbis [discussed this]. Rabbi Levi said: Everyone in whose regard haya is stated saw [the emergence of] a new world. Rabbi Shmuel said: They are five: Noah – yesterday [during the Flood], “stones were worn away by water” (Job 14:19), as Rabbi Levi said in the name of Rabbi Yoḥanan: Even the lower millstone was obliterated in the water. Then you read: “The sons of Noah who emerged from the ark”? (Genesis 9:18). This [change] is bewildering! However, it indicates that he saw [the emergence of] a new world. Joseph – “they tortured his legs with chains” (Psalms 105:18), but now, “Joseph was the ruler”! (Genesis 42:6). However, it indicates that he saw a new world. Moses – yesterday, he was fleeing from Pharaoh, and now he was drowning him in the sea! However, it indicates that he saw a new world. Job – yesterday, “He spills my bile onto the ground” (Job 16:13), and now, “the Lord added to Job double of all that he had before”! (Job 42:10). However, it indicates that he saw a new world. Mordekhai – yesterday he was destined for hanging, and now he is hanging his hangers! However, it indicates that he saw a new world. The other Rabbis say: Everyone in whose regard haya is stated, he fed others and sustained them. Noah fed and sustained [the animals] all twelve months, as it is stated: “And you, take for you [from all food that is eaten…and it shall be for you and for them for food]” (Genesis 6:21). Joseph – “Joseph provided for his father and his brothers” (Genesis 47:12). Moses fed and sustained Israel for forty years in the wilderness. Job – “I ate my bread alone, and an orphan did not partake of it?” (Job 31:17). This was meant as a rhetorical question. Mordekhai fed and sustained others. Rabbi Yudan said: One time he went around to all the wet nurses, but did not immediately find a wet nurse for Esther, and he nursed her himself. Rabbi Berekhya and Rabbi Abahu said in the name of Rabbi Eliezer: Milk came into him [his breasts] and he nursed her. When Rabbi Abahu expounded this in public, the audience laughed as he spoke [of a man producing milk]. He said to them: But is it not [stated in] a mishna: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says: The milk of a male is not subject to ritual impurity.”

paragraphs.text: Bereshit Rabbah 67:2: ““Isaac was overcome with great trembling” – Rabbi Ḥama ben Rabbi Ḥanina said: “Great” – more than the trembling that he trembled atop the altar. He said: “Who [then], is” the one who became an intermediary between me and the Omnipresent so that Jacob would receive the blessings? He said it regarding Rebecca. Rabbi Yoḥanan said: One who has two sons, one leaving and one entering, trembles? I wonder. It is, rather, that when Esau entered to his father, Gehenna entered with him. Rabbi Aḥa said: The walls of the house began seething. That is what is written: “Who then [mi efo],” who is that who is destined to be baked here, is it me, or my son Jacob? The Holy One blessed be He said to him: ‘It is neither you nor your son, but rather, “he who hunted game.”’ “He who hunted game” – Rabbi Elazar bar Shimon said: Hunter, how did they trap you? Conqueror of gates, how are your gates conquered and ruined? That is what is written: “The deceitful will not scorch [yaḥarokh] his prey” (Proverbs 12:27). The Rabbis say: The Holy One blessed be He does not delay [yeaḥer] and does not extend [yaarikh] for the deceitful one and his deceit. Rabbi Eliezer the son of Rabbi Yosei said: What is “will not scorch [lo yaḥarokh]”? the Holy One Blessed be He does not extend [yaarikh] for the deceitful one and his deceit, as Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said: That entire day, Esau was trapping gazelles and binding them, and an angel came and untied them, [trapping] birds, and tied their wings, and an angel would come and free them. Why to that extent? “But the wealth of a worthy [yakar] man is precious” (Proverbs 12:27) – so that Jacob, who was the glory of [yekaro] the world, would come and take the blessings, as from the outset of the world they were designated [ḥarutzot] for him. Rabbi Ḥanina bar Pappa asked Rabbi Aḥa, he said to him: ‘What is what is written: “But the wealth of a worthy [yakar] man is precious [ḥarutz]”?’ He said: ‘It is designated [ḥarutza] in the hands of the righteous, who do not receive in this world any of the glory they have coming to them in the World to Come.’ “And I ate from all [mikol]” – Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Neḥemya, Rabbi Yehuda says: Of everything [mikol] that was created during the six days of Creation. Rabbi Neḥemya says: Of all [mikol] the goodness that is reserved for the World to Come. He [Esau] said to him [Isaac]: ‘What was the main course that he fed you?’ He said to him: ‘I do not know, but I tasted the taste of bread, the taste of meat, the taste of fish, the taste of grasshoppers, the taste of all the delicacies of the world.’ Rabbi Berekhya said: When he [Isaac] mentioned meat, he [Esau] immediately cried. He said: ‘He fed me one bowl of lentils and took my birthright. You, to whom he fed meat, all the more so.’ Rabbi Levi said: Because our patriarch Isaac was afraid and saying: ‘Did I, perhaps, not act properly, in that I rendered one who was not firstborn, firstborn?’ When he said: “He took my birthright” (Genesis 27:36), he said: ‘I gave the blessing properly.’ Rabbi Elazar said: Ratification of a document is only by its signatories, so that you will not say that had Jacob not deceived Isaac, he would not have received the blessings. The verse states: “Indeed, he shall be blessed.””

: ““Isaac was overcome with great trembling” – Rabbi Ḥama ben Rabbi Ḥanina said: “Great” – more than the trembling that he trembled atop the altar. He said: “Who [then], is” the one who became an intermediary between me and the Omnipresent so that Jacob would receive the blessings? He said it regarding Rebecca. Rabbi Yoḥanan said: One who has two sons, one leaving and one entering, trembles? I wonder. It is, rather, that when Esau entered to his father, Gehenna entered with him. Rabbi Aḥa said: The walls of the house began seething. That is what is written: “Who then [mi efo],” who is that who is destined to be baked here, is it me, or my son Jacob? The Holy One blessed be He said to him: ‘It is neither you nor your son, but rather, “he who hunted game.”’ “He who hunted game” – Rabbi Elazar bar Shimon said: Hunter, how did they trap you? Conqueror of gates, how are your gates conquered and ruined? That is what is written: “The deceitful will not scorch [yaḥarokh] his prey” (Proverbs 12:27). The Rabbis say: The Holy One blessed be He does not delay [yeaḥer] and does not extend [yaarikh] for the deceitful one and his deceit. Rabbi Eliezer the son of Rabbi Yosei said: What is “will not scorch [lo yaḥarokh]”? the Holy One Blessed be He does not extend [yaarikh] for the deceitful one and his deceit, as Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said: That entire day, Esau was trapping gazelles and binding them, and an angel came and untied them, [trapping] birds, and tied their wings, and an angel would come and free them. Why to that extent? “But the wealth of a worthy [yakar] man is precious” (Proverbs 12:27) – so that Jacob, who was the glory of [yekaro] the world, would come and take the blessings, as from the outset of the world they were designated [ḥarutzot] for him. Rabbi Ḥanina bar Pappa asked Rabbi Aḥa, he said to him: ‘What is what is written: “But the wealth of a worthy [yakar] man is precious [ḥarutz]”?’ He said: ‘It is designated [ḥarutza] in the hands of the righteous, who do not receive in this world any of the glory they have coming to them in the World to Come.’ “And I ate from all [mikol]” – Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Neḥemya, Rabbi Yehuda says: Of everything [mikol] that was created during the six days of Creation. Rabbi Neḥemya says: Of all [mikol] the goodness that is reserved for the World to Come. He [Esau] said to him [Isaac]: ‘What was the main course that he fed you?’ He said to him: ‘I do not know, but I tasted the taste of bread, the taste of meat, the taste of fish, the taste of grasshoppers, the taste of all the delicacies of the world.’ Rabbi Berekhya said: When he [Isaac] mentioned meat, he [Esau] immediately cried. He said: ‘He fed me one bowl of lentils and took my birthright. You, to whom he fed meat, all the more so.’ Rabbi Levi said: Because our patriarch Isaac was afraid and saying: ‘Did I, perhaps, not act properly, in that I rendered one who was not firstborn, firstborn?’ When he said: “He took my birthright” (Genesis 27:36), he said: ‘I gave the blessing properly.’ Rabbi Elazar said: Ratification of a document is only by its signatories, so that you will not say that had Jacob not deceived Isaac, he would not have received the blessings. The verse states: “Indeed, he shall be blessed.””

This teaches that the Holy One, Blessed be He, is scrupulous with those around Him, i.e., the righteous, even to the extent of a hairsbreadth [hasa’ara], so that even minor transgressions elicit a severe punishment. Rabbi Neḥunya says: The same idea may be learned from here, in the following verse: “A God dreaded in the great council of the holy ones, and feared by all those that surround Him” (Psalms 89:8), indicating that God is most careful and exacting with those that surround Him, i.e., the righteous.”

paragraphs.text: Shabbat 86b:5: “The Sages taught: On the sixth day of the month of Sivan, the Ten Commandments were given to the Jewish people. Rabbi Yosei says: On the seventh day of the month. Rava said: Everyone agrees that the Jews came to the Sinai desert on the New Moon, as it is written here: “In the third month after the children of Israel were gone forth out of the land of Egypt, the same day came they into the wilderness of Sinai” (Exodus 19:1), without elaborating what day it was. And it is written there: “This month shall be to you the beginning of months; it shall be the first month of the year to you” (Exodus 12:2). Just as there, the term “this” is referring to the New Moon, so too, here the term is referring to the New Moon. And similarly, everyone agrees that the Torah was given to the Jewish people on Shabbat, as it is written here in the Ten Commandments: “Remember the Shabbat day to keep it holy” (Exodus 20:8), and it is written there: “And Moses said to the people: Remember this day, in which you came out from Egypt, out of the house of bondage, for by strength of hand the Lord brought you out from this place; there shall be no leaven eaten” (Exodus 13:3). Just as there, the mitzva of remembrance was commanded on the very day of the Exodus, so too, here the mitzva of remembrance was commanded on the very day of Shabbat. Where Rabbi Yosei and the Sages disagree is with regard to the determination of the month, meaning which day of the week was established as the New Moon. Rabbi Yosei held: The New Moon was established on the first day of the week, and on the first day of the week He did not say anything to them due to the weariness caused by the journey. On the second day of the week, He said to them: “And you shall be to Me a kingdom of priests and a holy nation; these are the words that you shall speak to the children of Israel” (Exodus 19:6).”
